# Trenith Tools — factual reference

Trenith Tools is a free global utility platform operated by Trenith Technologies Private Limited, CIN U62099TS2026PTC216554, registered in India.

The global hostname is https://tools.trenith.com and the India-focused hostname is https://tools.trenith.in. Each deployment should use a self-referencing canonical and reciprocal en / en-IN hreflang links.

The platform contains three kinds of workflow. Device tools use browser APIs or locally loaded WebAssembly and do not intentionally send selected source files to Trenith. Public Source tools send a user-entered public URL to a Trenith route for the requested scan or retrieval. BYOK tools send user-initiated requests to the provider the user connects; provider terms and billing apply.

Trenith Watch Together is a separate free real-time feature for authorized OTT web playback. Every participant opens the title through their own provider account. A Manifest V3 browser companion (1.1.0) synchronizes play, pause, seek and playback rate — through the page's own player API on Netflix and the HTML5 element elsewhere; it does not screen-capture, download, decrypt or retransmit the title. Launch adapters cover YouTube, Netflix, Prime Video and JioHotstar, while other listed providers use an honestly labeled generic HTML5 beta. Sync protocol 2 aligns every room clock with the signaling server, projects remote positions for latency before applying them, re-broadcasts the host position every five seconds while playing, shows each participant's drift in the roster with a one-click resync, lets hosts hand over, remove a participant or lock the room, and promotes the longest-present guest automatically when the host is silent for 45 seconds. Native streaming mobile and TV apps are not controlled. Room chat, reactions, playback state and WebRTC negotiation are AES-GCM encrypted in the browser and expire from signaling storage; temporary display names, roles, token hashes and connection timestamps remain operational metadata. Optional camera/microphone media uses WebRTC and is not recorded by Trenith. Rooms expire after six hours, support up to 25 synchronized participants and limit live media to six.

The metadata remover accepts files and folders, inventories recognized metadata, removes supported fields, rescans the output and offers individual or ZIP downloads. Cleaning is routed per format: the embedded ExifTool engine rewrites images and camera RAW formats while preserving the colour profile and orientation; every audio and video container (MP3, FLAC, Ogg, Opus, WAV, AIFF, M4A, WMA, WavPack, AC3, MP4, MOV, M4V, 3GP, MKV, WebM, AVI, MPEG-TS, FLV and more) is rewritten as a lossless FFmpeg stream copy with tags, chapters, cover art and encoder signatures dropped and track languages restored; a document rewriter strips PDF information dictionaries and XMP, anonymizes annotation and form authors and physically removes orphaned objects left by earlier saves; Word, Excel and PowerPoint packages lose core, extended and custom properties, people lists, thumbnails, revision identifiers, comment and tracked-change authors, template and mail-merge links, absolute save paths and threaded-comment identities; OpenDocument, EPUB, SVG, HTML and RTF files are rewritten directly; ZIP archives are cleaned recursively, and media embedded inside any document is cleaned by its own engine. Every output is rescanned and reported by risk category (location, identity, device, timestamps, software). It does not promise removal of visible content, steganography, proprietary databases or every application-specific trace.

Free on-device SEO tools include a SERP snippet preview with character and approximate pixel checks for titles and descriptions, and a keyword density analyzer reporting word counts, reading time, estimated readability, repeated phrases and the questions a text answers. Both run entirely in the browser.

The AI Studio runs every workflow with whichever provider connection exists and states which provider produces the strongest result. Text-capable keys from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or OpenRouter run all text workflows and produce structured production plans for media workflows. Vision-capable keys can read text from JPEG, PNG or WebP scans. Text to speech plays through built-in browser voices with no key, while an ElevenLabs key returns downloadable MP3 audio. Compatible custom endpoints can run full media jobs.

The audio joiner accepts files and folders in a user-controlled order. It first uses native browser decoding and automatically retries rejected files with a locally loaded FFmpeg WebAssembly compatibility engine. Smaller compatible jobs are joined in memory. Jobs over the defined file-count or size threshold use a compatible desktop File System Access API, preflight files independently, report unreadable names, optionally skip unreadable files, and stream PCM output directly to a WAV or RF64-compatible destination. There is no artificial file-count quota, but disk space, browser support and codecs remain practical constraints.

The audio converter produces MP3, M4A/AAC, WAV, FLAC, ALAC, AIFF, Ogg Vorbis, Opus, WebM, WavPack, AC3 and WMA output on the device, for single files or whole folders with a one-ZIP download, with sample-rate, channel and bit-depth options and tags plus cover art carried over. Audio trimming cuts without re-encoding in the source format or exports to any format; volume adjustment exports to any format. Video tools convert between MP4, WebM, MKV and MOV (a lossless remux whenever the source codecs already fit the container, otherwise H.264 or VP8 encoding with quality, resolution, frame-rate and rotation control), compress by quality or target size, trim with keyframe-exact lossless or frame-accurate cuts, extract audio as a bit-for-bit copy when the codec matches, and render palette-optimized GIFs; the video joiner concatenates losslessly when clips match. Video re-encoding is single-threaded WebAssembly and slower than real time for long high-resolution clips. PDF tools merge, split, extract, rotate, number, watermark, recompress embedded images at a chosen quality and resolution while leaving the text layer untouched, render pages to JPG, PNG or WebP and extract text through pdf.js. Image tools open HEIC, TIFF, SVG and AVIF and export JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, ICO and TIFF, singly or in batch; Images to PDF accepts JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, TIFF, GIF, BMP and SVG. The public audio scanner can package discovered authorized files into a ZIP without bypassing source controls.

The public `/status` page explains the engine and dependency for every workspace. `/changelog` and `/feed.xml` publish release history, and `/api/tools` exposes a CORS-readable JSON catalog.

Trenith Tools is free. Revenue can come from Trenith service inquiries, clearly disclosed contextual sponsorship or affiliate relationships, and consented aggregate analytics or campaign measurement. Trenith does not sell personal data or use file contents, private metadata, API keys, prompts or outputs for advertising.

Minimum age is 18. Privacy contacts are privacy@trenith.in, legal@trenith.in and grevience@trenith.in. The public Privacy Notice, Terms, Cookie Policy, Privacy Choices, Security, Subprocessors, Copyright and Accessibility pages are controlling sources for current site practices.
